Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a run-of-show into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme run-of-show and deliver a live timeline: Wedding Reception Run Sheet — Ashgrove Barn for 90 guests, three courses
Resource limits: one kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, two servers on the floor, one dance floor.
Everything must be finished by band's last set.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Wedding Reception Run Sheet — Ashgrove Barn, 90 guests

The ceremony breaks at four o'clock and this sheet starts there. One kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, two servers on the floor, one band. The planner owns the room call; the MC owns everything that goes through the microphone. Nothing on the pass overlaps: the kitchen plates one course at a time and the floor waits for it.

Room
Flip the ceremony room to reception seating: 45 minutes, chairs out, rounds in, linen on.
Dress the tables with centrepieces, place cards and candles; 15 minutes once the flip is done.
Seat the guests when the planner calls the room; 15 minutes to get 90 people down.

Foyer
Open the bar as soon as the ceremony breaks; 20 minutes to set and pour the first round.
Pass canapes in the foyer from twenty minutes in, and keep passing for forty minutes to an hour, however long the photographs take.
Call the room to dinner once the canapes are done; 5 minutes.

Kitchen
Starters plate up fifteen minutes after the room starts seating; 15 minutes on the pass.
Mains go on the pass five minutes after the starter plates are cleared; 30 minutes.
Dessert plates up the moment the cake is cut; 15 minutes.

Floor
Serve the starters; 10 minutes.
Clear the starters twenty minutes after they go out; 10 minutes.
Serve the mains; 15 minutes.
Clear the mains forty minutes after they go out; 10 minutes.
Serve the dessert; 10 minutes.

Programme
Welcome toast as soon as the guests are seated; 5 minutes on the microphone.
First dance once the main plates are cleared; 5 minutes.
Speeches when the MC cues them: two or three of them, fifteen minutes total, twenty-five at the outside.
Cut the cake straight after the speeches; 10 minutes.
Dancing starts ten minutes after the dessert is served and runs until the band's last set.

Notes for the day
The photographs are the only thing we do not control, so the canape window is the slack in the sheet: if the couple are late back from the orchard the bar carries it. Everything downstream of the room call is fixed. If the speeches run long, the kitchen holds the dessert rather than plating it early — the pass is the bottleneck and a plated dessert sitting under a lamp is worse than a five minute gap on the floor.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

This is a live wedding-reception run-of-show for 90 guests at Ashgrove Barn, starting when the ceremony breaks at 4:00 pm and needing to finish no later than the band’s last set; the source does not state the last set time, so the exact deadline is unspecified. It sequences a room flip and table dressing, bar opening and a flexible canape window that absorbs photo delays, guest seating, three courses plated and served in strict sequence, and programme moments including the welcome toast, first dance, speeches, cake cutting, and dancing. The constraints are hard single resources: one kitchen pass means only one course can be plated at a time and the floor waits; there is one bar, one microphone, one dance floor, one band, and two floor servers. Some work must be held or triggered at precise moments: the room call fixes everything downstream, starters begin relative to seating, mains wait for starters to clear, the first dance waits for main plates to clear, dessert plates only when the cake is cut, and if speeches run long the kitchen holds dessert rather than plating early.

```json
{
  "summary": "This is a live wedding-reception run-of-show for 90 guests at Ashgrove Barn, starting when the ceremony breaks at 4:00 pm and needing to finish no later than the band’s last set; the source does not state the last set time, so the exact deadline is unspecified. It sequences a room flip and table dressing, bar opening and a flexible canape window that absorbs photo delays, guest seating, three courses plated and served in strict sequence, and programme moments including the welcome toast, first dance, speeches, cake cutting, and dancing. The constraints are hard single resources: one kitchen pass means only one course can be plated at a time and the floor waits; there is one bar, one microphone, one dance floor, one band, and two floor servers. Some work must be held or triggered at precise moments: the room call fixes everything downstream, starters begin relative to seating, mains wait for starters to clear, the first dance waits for main plates to clear, dessert plates only when the cake is cut, and if speeches run long the kitchen holds dessert rather than plating early.",
  "servesOrScale": "90 guests; 45 rounds; three courses",
  "deadline": "unspecified: finish by the band’s last set; sheet starts at 4:00 pm ceremony break",
  "constraints": [
    "one kitchen pass",
    "one bar",
    "one microphone",
    "one dance floor",
    "one band",
    "two servers on the floor",
    "no overlap on the kitchen pass",
    "courses plate and serve in sequence",
    "canape duration flexes with photographs",
    "room call fixes downstream timing",
    "dessert waits until cake is cut",
    "speeches may run longer than planned",
    "band last set time is not specified"
  ]
}
```

A track is one ordered lane of work: each step waits for the previous one by default, so overlapping activities must be split into different tracks. A step needs exactly one duration kind: `fixed` with seconds, `variable` with min/max/default, or `indefinite` that runs until the person ends it. A startTrigger is how a step begins: at the program clock, at an offset, after another step, after another step plus buffer, manually, on abort, or as a compound wait. Step IDs are global, because any trigger in any track may refer to any other step. A step’s `task` is the resource it occupies, and every used task needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry whose `maxConcurrent` caps simultaneous use. Repeated work should not be hand-copied into many steps or tracks; it uses `replicates` on one step, with `instances: "each"` for per-instance follow-ups, `instances: "all"` for the barrier, and `maxInFlight` when a holding-area limit should hold the upstream work.

Expected resource constraints:

- `kitchen_pass` — maxConcurrent `1` — one kitchen pass; only one course may be plated at a time.
- `bar` — maxConcurrent `1` — one bar; set/open/first-round work occupies the bar resource.
- `microphone` — maxConcurrent `1` — one microphone/MC-owned line; toast, speeches, and announcements cannot share it.
- `floor` — maxConcurrent `2` — two servers on the floor; floor service and canape-passing work draw from this two-person pool.
- `dance_floor` — maxConcurrent `1` — one dance floor; first dance and dancing cannot both occupy it.

I intend `actors: 1` because the prompt says this is a live run-of-show followed by one person; the “two servers on the floor” constraint is expressed as floor capacity via `maxConcurrent`, not as two separate timeline followers.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps; every task needs a resourceConstraint; stepIds are global; repeated work uses replicates with each/all chains and maxInFlight when appropriate.",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "kitchen_pass", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "bar", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "microphone", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "floor", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "dance_floor", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 1
}
```

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);
- `sourceSpan`: the exact words in the text you took it from, as `{"quote": "...", "occurrence": n}`, where n says which occurrence of those words you mean (1 for the first). Quote the text verbatim — do not paraphrase it;
- `inferred`: `true` for a step the text never states but the work needs anyway (preheating, thawing, resting, cooling, labelling, sound-check), with `"sourceSpan": null`. Keep these few and obvious.

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.
